analysis.title: Global Equities: Move From Defence to Offence, Start Buying Weakness
key_insights: UBS sales desk (Zain Nizami, 22-Oct-2026) argues the balance of risk is shifting from holding defensive exposure toward selectively buying weakness. Asia looks technically washed out while parts of Europe look overbought.
Defensive positioning and more aggressive downside expressions worked over the past two to three days. Several of those moves now look stretched on price action and positioning metrics.

Thursday's APAC session was weak, and the size of the risk-off move looked disproportionate to the post-market earnings and geopolitical information available. HSTECH is 23% below its 200-day moving average with an RSI of 27.
The CSI 300 has an RSI of 23.9, matching historical lows, while testing its weekly 200-day moving average.
Parts of Europe are overbought. Roughly 40% of the SMI and 25% of the DAX (driven largely by Insurance and SAP-related exposure) have RSI readings above 70.

The cross-asset backdrop is still elevated oil, wider OAT-Bund spreads and higher sovereign yields. Yields are now easing somewhat amid a flight to safety. Political and geopolitical headlines have accelerated these moves.
Some correlations are re-emerging. Relative-value relationships, particularly Semis versus Software, are approaching extreme levels.
The Hang Seng registered a 95% down day and Hong Kong absorbed most of the selling, though weakness was broad. KOSPI had 627 decliners against 152 advancers.

With sentiment, positioning and known macro headwinds largely reflected in prices, UBS says it is appropriate to move away from an outright bearish and defensive stance. Levels remain uncomfortable, and it suggests pricing forward 'what-if' scenarios.
Conditions do not yet justify a full risk-on 'green light', but risk/reward increasingly favours buying weakness over selling strength.

This does not yet look like market-wide capitulation. Net exposures have fallen but gross exposure, particularly in the US, remains elevated. The next source of pain may be rising correlations and crowded sector positioning, including a reversal in price relationships and breadth against rising short interest.

US equity short books have built up sharply in absolute terms and versus prior years. UBS reads this as a sign that much of the positioning adjustment is behind us, and the segment is more prone to squeezes than gaps lower.
UBS high-touch flow has been situational and idiosyncratic over earnings, and the overwhelming defensive flow has stopped.

Within tech, de-grossing of semis has accelerated and started to reach hyperscalers. The desk finds it tempting to sell hyperscalers and cover semis, or to play a ratioed relative. It says semiconductor stocks look interesting versus broader tech and software.

sector_views.rationale: Semis look interesting versus broader tech and software after accelerated de-grossing, and Semis vs Software relative value is near extreme levels.
Semis versus Software relative-value relationships are approaching extreme levels, and the desk prefers covering semis over software and hyperscalers.
De-grossing has started to reach hyperscalers, and the desk finds it tempting to sell them and cover semis.

trade_ideas.description: Long semiconductors versus short hyperscalers or software, via a ratioed relative trade
trade_ideas.rationale: Semis have been de-grossed heavily while hyperscalers are only starting to be de-grossed, and Semis vs Software relative value is near extreme levels.
trade_ideas.risk: Rising correlations, crowded sector positioning and a reversal in price relationships and market breadth.

trade_ideas.description: Buy weakness in oversold Asian equities (HSTECH, CSI 300) and move away from defensive positioning
trade_ideas.rationale: Extreme oversold readings (HSTECH RSI 27, CSI 300 RSI 23.9) and a risk-off move that looks disproportionate to the available information.
trade_ideas.risk: This is not yet a classic capitulation, and gross exposure is still elevated.

tension_points.bull_case: Asia is technically washed out (HSTECH RSI 27, CSI 300 RSI 23.9). Macro headwinds look largely priced, defensive flow has stopped, and large US short books make squeezes more likely than gaps lower.
tension_points.bear_case: This is not a classic capitulation. US gross exposure is still elevated and concentrated, and rising correlations and a reversal in market breadth against increasing short interest could cause further pain.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A reversal in established price relationships and market breadth, with rising correlations and crowded sector positioning unwinding.
